protocol.stepSettingsForReferenceTools: A reference tool runs at its own converged setting (stated with its results, with the change a finer setting makes); the three settings are FFM's side of the comparison. A tool that exposes step control may also be run at the same three settings.
protocol.sensitivities: Cases with sensitivities report the 6x6 STM and the parameter columns at each sample; scored as the largest relative difference of a column (position rows and velocity rows apart), as tests/lib/orekitCases.mjs scoreJacobians. Parameters are per unit Cd*A/m, Cr*A/m, the Cd*A/m rate, and the in-track acceleration.

cause.statement: GMAT gtd7 excludes anomalous oxygen; FFM and Orekit use gtd7d drag-effective density. A constant Cd multiplier is an approximation to the varying density ratio: the corrected trajectory is the measured residual, not a claim of exact model identity.

stm.statement: STM and Cd*A/m, Cr*A/m, Cd*A/m-rate, and in-track-acceleration sensitivity agreement is reported as maximum relative column difference, separately for position and velocity rows. Native aerodynamic state partials use central finite differences at 10 m position and 0.01 m/s velocity perturbations, also used by the time-varying-drag adapter. The native cannonball SRP partial omits the eclipse-attenuation position gradient; its effect is conditional on encountering eclipse transitions, not every SRP case. R2 STM omissions record unavailable native non-Schwarzschild partials. Every exported sensitivity is included where its variational case is supported; the shared export defines no STM pass/fail threshold.

cause.statement: Basilisk MsisAtmosphere uses spherical altitude and geocentric latitude, and below 500 km selects gtd7 without anomalous oxygen. The export/FFM use WGS84 geodetic coordinates and gtd7d density. Changing only atmosphere coordinates removes the kilometer-scale discrepancy; additionally supplying the installed wheel's native gtd7d density removes the meter-scale residual and passes every unchanged FFM tolerance. This is a measured native model-setting limitation, not evidence of an FFM defect.

cause.statement: Basilisk MsisAtmosphere uses spherical altitude and geocentric latitude, and below 500 km selects gtd7 without anomalous oxygen. The export/FFM use WGS84 geodetic coordinates and gtd7d density. Changing only atmosphere coordinates removes the kilometer-scale discrepancy; additionally supplying the installed wheel's native gtd7d density removes the meter-scale residual and passes every unchanged FFM tolerance. This is a measured native model-setting limitation, not evidence of an FFM defect.

toolCauses.label: Nyx NRLMSISE-00 port
toolCauses.statement: With the published NRLMSISE-00 formulas and the WGS84 Earth shape, the five missed cases are about 0.05 m from FFM, all below the unchanged 0.1 m limit. The exact corrected residuals are recorded per case. The port defect and the cached runner Earth-shape mismatch are separated in the per-case diagnostics; they do not indicate an FFM defect.

toolCauses.label: Nyx variational equation
toolCauses.statement: The STM comparison is not usable as an FFM check: Nyx uses the step-start ctx.stm and computes stm * grad, instead of grad * stage_stm, while the RK stages retain the same context.

toolCauses.label: GMAT anomalous oxygen
toolCauses.statement: GMAT gtd7 excludes anomalous oxygen; FFM and Orekit use gtd7d drag-effective density. The day-mean density ratio times the independently stored drag effect accounts for the meter-scale gap. A constant Cd multiplier is an approximation to the varying density ratio: the corrected trajectory is the measured residual, not a claim of exact model identity.
